LAREDO, Texas — Laredo’s first binational anti-bullying poetry contest takes the stage today, Sunday, Oct. 25, at 2 p.m. at the Laredo Independent School District Performing Arts Center, according to KGNS.

The event is hosted by Laredo Proud Inc. and community partners, and it invites participants to express anti-bullying messages in English, Spanish, or any language of their choice — a deliberately binational, bilingual frame for a border community where many families live their lives in two languages.

Each winner will receive a $200 prize, and attendees are encouraged to wear Halloween costumes, giving the afternoon a festive, family-friendly feel in the run-up to Halloween.

The contest lands during National Bullying Prevention Month, when LISD itself has been marking Unity Day and urging students to wear orange and stand together against bullying. A poetry contest is a fitting local twist on that message: instead of lectures about bullying, young people get the microphone and the chance to say, in their own words and their own language, what kindness should look like.

Registration was open ahead of the event. Families heading to the LISD Performing Arts Center this afternoon can expect an event built around student voices — and, given the costume encouragement, a few ghosts and superheroes in the audience too.

Sources: KGNS (Laredo) reporting on the binational anti-bullying poetry contest, Oct. 25, 2026.

title: Laredo hosts first binational anti-bullying poetry contest today at LISD Performing Arts Center
